About

Sharing research with academic, policy, and public audiences at NCA 2025, Denver, CO

Neha Gour is a Ph.D. candidate in Science Communication at George Mason University and an affiliated researcher with the Center for Climate Change Communication. She is currently an Institute for a Sustainable Earth Summer Fellow with The Nature Conservancy. Her work examines the intersections of AI infrastructure, climate change, public health, and public policy. Using quantitative methods, she generates and evaluates empirical evidence to inform policy, public communication, and decision-making.

Her research spans the health implications of data center expansion, the role of health professionals as climate communicators, and how news coverage of climate change as a health issue has evolved over the past decade across the United States, India, and China. Her dissertation uses cross-national survey data from the United States, India, and China to examine how trusted opinion leaders shape public understanding of climate change and health. She works closely with policymakers, journalists, industry, and community stakeholders to translate research into evidence-based strategies that support both technological innovation and community well-being.

Neha has led and contributed to research, policy communication, and knowledge management initiatives with international organizations, research institutes, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations, including The Nature Conservancy, the Government of the City of Fairfax, Virginia; the World Health Organization (WHO); UNESCO; the Wellcome Trust; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark; Oxford Policy Management; Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy; the Centre for Policy Research; and the Ministry of Education, Government of India.

✦ Recent Publication

Health implications of the rapid rise of data centers in Virginia: An exploratory assessment

Gour, N., Ortiz, L., Maibach, E.

Frontiers in Climate, 8, 1648912 · 2026

24K+ Views 2.5K Downloads 158 Altmetric Score Read in 60+ Countries 20+ Media Coverage 10+ Invited Talks
Driven by advances in cloud computing, cryptocurrency, and artificial intelligence, the rapid proliferation of data centers may pose severe human and planetary health risks. This paper, to the best of our knowledge, is the first-of-its-kind assessment of the potential health implications associated with data centers.
